lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1711 — the escort has to go somewhere

Step 3d. OTA-1710 audited the fetch counter, the staged beats and the wealth
gate, and said out loud that ESCORT was not reached — 29 of the 65 faction
contracts, the largest family in the game, whose ledger is a party of bodies
taking collateral damage across real fights rather than a number you can set.

⚠ THE FIRST PROBE FOUND THAT THE WORK WAS OPTIONAL.

Accept an escort from an agent, hand it straight back to THAT SAME AGENT
without moving a step:

    ✦ Faction contract complete — The Survey Line. +70 TC, +8 rep.

The party spawns at full health, so the scaled-pay multiplier is 1, and nothing
on the turn-in path ever asked where anybody had been. `send word` did the same
thing from anywhere on the map. Every one of the 29 could be closed for full
pay and full rep without escorting anyone anywhere.

Two refusals now, and both mirror rules this file already keeps:

  · YOU CANNOT COURIER PEOPLE. The clause beside it already refuses to mail a
    FETCH deed because "you cannot mail the goods". An escort is the same
    objection with more of it.

  · YOU CANNOT HAND A PARTY BACK ON THE SPOT YOU COLLECTED THEM FROM.

⚠ THE RULE IS DELIBERATELY THE WEAKEST ONE THAT CLOSES IT. Every escort
objective reads "escort them to a <faction> agent" — not to a named place, and
none of the 29 carries a `targetLocationName` or an `objectiveLocationId`. So
there is no destination to check against, and inventing one would be redesigning
29 contracts on my own authority. What can be said without inventing anything is
that the party has to have GONE somewhere.

It reads `acceptedAtCell`, which is already stamped at accept and already read
one line below the turn-in for the long-haul bonus — so it needs no new state,
and the gate cannot disagree with the reward that prices the same walk. It FAILS
OPEN on a contract accepted before this OTA: a save with no stamped cell
delivers exactly as it does today, because stranding a party the player is
already carrying would be a worse bug than the one being fixed.

And the positive case is tested as hard as the refusal, because a rule that
closes an exploit by making 29 contracts unfinishable is not a fix: walk them to
a different cell and the contract completes and pays MORE than its base, since
the long-haul bonus reads the same journey. The refusal also leaves the contract
on the slate — refused, not failed. Nobody loses a party for asking too early.

⚠ TWO THINGS THE AUDIT FOUND AND DID NOT CHANGE, both written into the suite.

A DEAD POOL PAYS IN FULL on an all-or-nothing contract, because the pay code
skips the scaling for that mode entirely and OTA-964's "or lose everything when
the pool dies" is not in that branch. It is UNREACHABLE IN PLAY — the only path
that damages a pool fails the contract the moment it hits zero and drops the
record, so there is no contract left to hand in — and I did not rewrite pay code
on the strength of a state I had to build by hand. The unreachability is pinned
instead, so a future damage path that forgets to fail the quest gets named
rather than quietly making the full payout reachable.

PARKING PROTECTS THE PARTY BY DESIGN. `setFactionQuestActive(id, false)` parks
them — OTA-962's own words, "off the HUD, no combat damage" — so walking every
fight with the party parked and delivering them pristine is currently the
optimal play, and the collateral mechanic is opt-in. That is a balance call
rather than a defect, so this OTA does not touch it; it is recorded because the
alternative is that nobody notices until a player does. The delivery gate is
unaffected either way: parked or not, they still have to have gone somewhere.

⚠ AND IT MOVED WHAT "COURIERABLE" MEANS, which two suites caught. The audit
harness accepts and hands in on the spot, so all 29 escorts failed it — fixed
the way that harness already handles a fetch requirement: satisfy the
precondition (stand the pickup cell elsewhere) rather than simulate the walk.
And OTA-1403's `courierableDeed()` selected "no fetch, no stages", which is
exactly the shape of an escort — EVERY stage-less, fetch-less contract in the
catalog is one, so that selector could now only pick something a runner may not
carry. What a runner can still carry is a staged deed whose work is behind it:
goods cannot be mailed, people cannot be mailed, and what is left is the
contract whose only remaining act is the word itself. That test's claim is
untouched; only the deed it is made on.
